preamble: Unrounding and lowering of open-mid [ɔ] to the open back vowel [ɑ]. In the cot–caught merger of Western American English, the THOUGHT vowel /ɔ/ of caught, dawn and stalk merged with the LOT vowel, which had already merged with PALM in the father–bother merger, so that the merged vowel is [ɑ] and caught rhymes with cot. Other merging accents reach different targets: Scottish English merges towards [ɔ] and Boston towards [ɒ].

examples.from: caught with the THOUGHT vowel /ɔ/ (kept in non-merging General American /kɔt/)
